```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash

TMP_DIR="/tmp"

# Make sure the target really exists and is readable
if [[ ! -d $TMP_DIR ]]; then
    echo "❌ Target directory '$TMP_DIR' doesn't exist."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Counting lines in each file found under $TMP_DIR …"

# Loop over *regular* files – skip sockets, pipes, devices, dirs…
while IFS= read -r -d '' FILEPATH ; do
    # Grab just the basename so the output looks tidy
    BASENAME=$(basename -- "$FILEPATH")

    # `wc -l` gives the line count; suppress the filename because we’ll add it ourselves
    LINE_COUNT=$(wc -l <"$FILEPATH")
    
    printf "%30s : %8d\n" "$BASENAME" "$LINE_COUNT"
done <   <(find "$TMP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0)

echo "✅ Done!"
```

| Step | Command |
|------|---------|

| 2️⃣ Find plain files (`-type f`) in `/tmp`, depth ≤ 1 | `find "$TMP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0` |
| 3️⃣ Read each pathname safely (handles spaces/newlines) | `IFS= read -r -d '' FILEPATH` |
| 4️⃣ Count lines without printing the filename again | `wc -l <"$FILEPATH"` |
| 5️⃣ Print nicely formatted result | `printf "%30s : %8d\n" ...` |

> ⚠️ **Tip:**  
> • If you also care about text‐only files, consider adding `-iname '*.txt'` or similar filters.  
> • Binary files may produce misleading counts—use `grep -I` or `LC_ALL=C tr -dc '\n' <file | wc -l` if you’re worried about non‑text data.

```bash

    done
' _ {} +
```
